Source step. This call materializes the first CBOR object from the attacker-controlled slice handed in by the outer uSWID parser. In the exact witness that object is a one-pair root map whose key is `2` (`FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY`) and whose value is an 18-element array; the last element is a 647-pair entity map containing 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24`.

In the root-map loop, `fu_coswid_read_tag()` decodes the sole root key from step 1 as `FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY`, so `pairs[i].value` is the 18-element entity array and becomes the value forwarded to `fu_coswid_parse_one_or_many()` at line 609.

Because the forwarded `ENTITY` value is an array, the helper iterates it. On `j == 17`, `value` is the last entity map from step 1; `cbor_isa_map(value)` succeeds and line 361 calls `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity(value, ...)` on that exact map.

For that selected entity map, `g_new0` allocates a zeroed `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity`. In vulnerable source this object has only `FuCoswidEntityRole roles[6]` for role storage, and the local append counter `entity_role_cnt` starts at 0.

While iterating the 647 pairs in the selected entity map, 11 interleaved pairs have key 33 and scalar value 24. Each time the key decodes to `FU_COSWID_TAG_ROLE`, control enters this block with `pairs[i].value` still that attacker-supplied scalar.

For each of those 11 `ROLE` entries, `pairs[i].value` is a CBOR uint, so this condition is true and the parser takes the scalar branch. The separate array branch at lines 434-452, which contains the only `entity_role_cnt >= G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)` check, is skipped.
The scalar branch materializes role value 24 from each repeated pair. Vulnerable code accepts that raw uint as `FuCoswidEntityRole` without any range validation before storing it.

With the scalar branch selected, the first six executions of this store fill `entity->roles[0]` through `entity->roles[5]` and advance `entity_role_cnt` from 0 to 6. Nothing in this branch checks the six-slot extent allocated in step 4.
